subject.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `registerMemoryPromptPreparation(...)` as a public plugin SDK lifecycle contract after the repaired implementation proves all prompt surfaces and upgrade paths?
rationale: The branch adds a new public plugin API rather than only relocating Memory Wiki internals, and the protected `maintainer` label indicates this contract needs explicit human ownership.

options.title: Approve the API after repairs
options.body: Keep one generic async preparation seam, but land it only after all prompt callers, scoped-agent routing, cache reads, and real behavior proof are corrected.

options.title: Keep the refactor plugin-local
options.body: Avoid expanding the SDK by redesigning Memory Wiki around an existing lifecycle seam if that can preserve async state loading without a new public contract.

options.title: Pause for API design
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define the intended lifecycle, cancellation, ordering, and compatibility guarantees for async prompt preparation.

recommendation.title: Approve the API after repairs
recommendation.body: Keep one generic async preparation seam, but land it only after all prompt callers, scoped-agent routing, cache reads, and real behavior proof are corrected.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the proposed cross-plugin contract and its Memory Wiki consumer, though broader current-main ownership evidence remains incomplete.
